'''''Cyphostemma juttae''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the genus ''[[Cyphostemma]]''. It is a slow-growing  [[succulent]] [[caudex]] shrub native to northwestern and north-central Namibia.<ref name = powo/> It is well known as an [[ornamental plant]].

The plant is also known as '''wild grape''', '''tree grape''', '''Namibian grape''', '''droog-my-keel''',<ref>{{cite web|title=''Cyphostemma juttae''|work=PlantZAfrica.com|url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantcd/cyphastemjut.htm|access-date=2015-07-07|archive-date=13 January 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113155226/http://plantzafrica.com/plantcd/cyphastemjut.htm}}</ref> '''Jutta's botterboom''', and '''bastard cobas'''. The name "tree grape" comes from the grape-like fruits produced by the plant. These fruits are extremely poisonous, and should be avoided.
 
This species can reach {{convert|6|ft|m|abbr=off}} tall and has large shiny leaves. It is a deciduous plant. It grows in an arid region of summer-rainfall, and it loses its leaves in the dryer winter.<ref>{{cite news |title= Top 10 Ugly plants |url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gardening/gardeningpicturegalleries/5506103/Top-10-ugly-plants.html |access-date= 2009-07-17 | location=London | work=The Daily Telegraph |date=2009-06-11}}</ref>

The species was first described as ''Cissus juttae'' by [[Kurt Dinter]] and [[Ernest Friedrich Gilg]] in 1912. In 1967 [[Bernard Marie Descoings]] placed the species in genus ''Cyphostemma'' as ''C. juttae''.<ref name = powo/>
